_note: Money is Thuso Money: payments, payouts, wallets, vouchers, gifts, group wallets, claims and Market orders. Every write is idempotent with a key. MyThuso never holds a card number. Wave 2 contract; Waves 3 and 5 build.

doorsToAdd.why: The switching partner's claim responses are supplier callbacks; a door to add.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never holds a card number.
refusals.why: The provider's page takes it.

refusals.statement: A payout line does not name its own amount for a visit.
refusals.why: The share is packages/catalog/earnings.json's arithmetic.

refusals.statement: A suspension never touches money already earned.
refusals.why: Money does not subscribe to a suspension.

refusals.statement: A scheme receives nothing about a person's grant.
refusals.why: Money serves only the scheme's aggregate role.

refusals.statement: Nothing is charged without an idempotency key.
refusals.why: A retry is not a second charge.

refusals.statement: Money does not hear that event.
refusals.why: Money hears the billable state changes packages/catalog/events.json lists under moneyHears, and an event carrying a reference into the record is refused even when its type is on the list.

refusals.statement: No doctor's payout is scheduled while the fee is undecided.
refusals.why: The documents give a range for a doctor's per-case fee, not a price. packages/catalog/money.json holds the fee as null until somebody named decides it, and a payout worked out from a number nobody decided is a promise nobody made.

refusals.statement: No scheme or employer sees what one person paid.
refusals.why: A scheme and an employer are served in aggregate. A person's payment tells whoever reads it that a visit happened, and when.

refusals.statement: That door is locked until its switch-on conditions are evidenced.
refusals.why: Payment results and payout advice arrive only through the doors in packages/catalog/feeds.json, and none of their conditions is met. In development the simulated provider stands behind them, in process, and nothing from the network does.

refusals.statement: Cash is recorded against a finished visit, and this one has not finished.
refusals.why: A cash code entered before Care says the visit was billable would record money for a visit that may still not happen.

refusals.statement: This visit has no price Money can read yet, so nothing is charged.
refusals.why: appointment.booked@1 carries no service, so the payable it opens has no amount until visit.billable@1 names one. A charge against a payable with no catalogue price is an amount that came from the caller.

refusals.statement: A payout does not go down without a line naming the visit and the reason.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/earnings.json's every-deduction-is-named rule, enforced on the ledger rather than only drawn on the screen.

card, eft, debit-order, wallet or cash-otp.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never takes a card number; the provider's page does.
refusals.why: Refused before it is logged.

refusals.statement: That amount is not what is owed.
refusals.why: A payable's amount comes from the catalogue.

refusals.statement: Cash is reconciled with the patient's one-time code.
refusals.why: Cash leakage is a pilot measure.

refusals.statement: That key was already used for a different payment, so nothing was charged.
refusals.why: The same key twice is the same act once. The same key with a different payable, method or amount is not a retry, and treating it as one would either charge the wrong thing or hide a second charge.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: A payment is taken against Money's own payable, whose amount comes from the catalogue. A payment against nothing is an amount that came from somewhere else.

refusals.statement: That is not yours to pay.
refusals.why: A payable belongs to the person it was opened for. A gift or a sponsor pays through their own routes.

refusals.statement: That way of paying is not offered for this.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/money.json says which methods each kind of payable takes, and a wallet is not offered until one is built.

refusals.statement: This has already been paid. Nothing was charged again.
refusals.why: A second payment for a paid payable under a new key is a patient charged twice by somebody pressing a button twice.

The encounter claimed for.
The tariff code.
The coding, from Clinical, through the gateway.

refusals.statement: Nothing is claimed for an encounter a doctor has not signed.
refusals.why: A claim is for care that happened and was reviewed.

withdrawn.why: It carried ICD-10 codes to Money through the Passport gateway, and the gateway turned the clinical-content rule off for it. Finance sees a service code and an amount and never why the service was needed (packages/catalog/vetting.json, view-billing): the coding for a claim is assembled inside the record and clinical boundary and handed to the switching partner through a door, and Money records the billing side only.

routes.summary: Record the billing side of a claim: what is owed, its tariff code and the amount. Why the service was needed is coded inside the record and sent to the switch without passing through Money.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The payable the claim is for, Money's own.
The tariff or service code: what was done, never why.
The amount claimed, in cents.

refusals.statement: Nothing is claimed for care a doctor has not signed.
refusals.why: A claim is for care that happened and was reviewed; Money learns that from review.billable, never from the record.

refusals.statement: Money never receives why a service was needed.
refusals.why: Finance sees a service code and an amount. The diagnosis coding goes to the switching partner from inside the record.
